recipes.title: Schedule a dbt build with artifacts
recipes.summary: Run a pinned dbt adapter on a schedule and keep dbt target and log files as Dagu run artifacts.
recipes.author: dagucloud
prerequisites: A dbt project and profiles directory available to the Dagu worker
Warehouse credentials supplied through the dbt profile environment
recipes.workflow:
description: Run dbt build on a schedule and preserve dbt artifacts.
schedule: "0 4 * * *"

params:
  - name: project_dir
    default: /srv/dbt/project
  - name: profiles_dir
    default: /srv/dbt/profiles
  - name: target
    default: prod
  - name: threads
    type: integer
    default: 4
    minimum: 1
    maximum: 32

steps:
  - id: dbt_build
    action: dbt@v1
    with:
      projectDir: ${params.project_dir}
      profilesDir: ${params.profiles_dir}
      requirements:
        - dbt-postgres==1.9.0
      command: build
      target: ${params.target}
      threads: ${params.threads}
      failFast: true
      targetPath: ${context.paths.artifacts_dir}/dbt-target
      logPath: ${context.paths.artifacts_dir}/dbt-logs
      timeoutSeconds: 3600
recipes.readme:
# Schedule a dbt build with artifacts

Runs `dbt build` through the official `dbt@v1` Action and stores dbt target and log directories with the Dagu run.

## Prerequisites

- Dagu 2.13.0 or newer.
- A dbt project, profiles directory, and warehouse credentials available to the worker.

## Inputs and secrets

Configure `project_dir`, `profiles_dir`, `target`, and `threads`. Supply warehouse credentials through environment variables referenced by `profiles.yml`.

## What it changes

Runs the dbt models, tests, snapshots, and seeds selected by the project. Warehouse effects depend on the dbt project.

## Verify

Review the Dagu step result, `dbt-target/run_results.json`, and the dbt logs stored as artifacts.

## Recovery

Use the project's rollback or model-restoration procedure, correct the dbt failure, and rerun the workflow.

recipes.title: Back up a directory with rclone
recipes.summary: Copy a local directory to any rclone remote without deleting files at the destination.
recipes.author: dagucloud
prerequisites: An rclone remote configured for the Dagu user
Read access to the source directory
recipes.workflow:
description: Copy a local directory to an rclone remote without deleting destination files.
schedule: "0 3 * * *"

params:
  - name: source
    default: /srv/data
    description: Local directory to copy
  - name: destination
    default: backup:data
    description: rclone destination

steps:
  - id: copy
    action: rclone@v1
    with:
      command: copy
      source: ${params.source}
      destination: ${params.destination}
      checksum: true
      fastList: true
      transfers: 4
      stats: 30s
recipes.readme:
# Back up a directory with rclone

Uses the official `rclone@v1` Action to copy files to a configured remote. The `copy` operation updates and adds files but does not mirror deletions.

## Prerequisites

- Dagu 2.13.0 or newer.
- An rclone configuration available to the Dagu user.

## Inputs and secrets

Set `source` to the local directory and `destination` to an rclone path such as `backup:data`. Credentials remain in the rclone configuration.

## What it changes

Creates or updates destination objects. It does not delete destination files that no longer exist locally.

## Verify

Run `rclone check <source> <destination>` or inspect the destination after the first run.

## Recovery

Restore files with an rclone copy in the opposite direction. Remove unwanted destination files manually after review.

recipes.title: Alert when disk usage is high
recipes.summary: Check filesystem utilization on a schedule and notify Slack before a disk fills up.
recipes.author: dagucloud
prerequisites: df and awk
A Slack incoming webhook URL exposed through an environment-backed Dagu secret
recipes.workflow:
description: Notify Slack when a filesystem reaches its utilization threshold.
schedule: "*/15 * * * *"

params:
  - name: path
    default: /
  - name: threshold_percent
    type: integer
    default: 85
    minimum: 1
    maximum: 100

secrets:
  - name: SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL
    provider: env
    key: SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL

handler_on:
  failure:
    action: http.request
    with:
      method: POST
      url: ${env.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL}
      headers:
        Content-Type: application/json
      body: '{"text":"Disk usage for ${params.path} reached the ${params.threshold_percent}% alert threshold on the Dagu host."}'

steps:
  - id: check_usage
    run: |
      #!/bin/sh
      set -eu
      usage="$(df -P "${params.path}" | awk 'NR == 2 { gsub(/%/, "", $5); print $5 }')"
      printf 'Disk usage for %s: %s%%\n' "${params.path}" "$usage"
      test "$usage" -lt "${params.threshold_percent}"
recipes.readme:
# Alert when disk usage is high

Checks a filesystem every fifteen minutes and fails when utilization reaches the configured threshold. The failure handler sends a Slack message.

## Prerequisites

- Dagu 2.13.0 or newer with `df` and `awk`.
- A Slack incoming webhook.

## Inputs and secrets

Set `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` in the Dagu process environment. Configure `path` and `threshold_percent`.

## What it changes

Reads filesystem statistics and may send one Slack message. It never deletes files.

## Verify

Run once with the normal threshold, then temporarily lower it below current usage to test the notification.

## Recovery

Free or expand storage, restore the threshold, and rerun the check.

recipes.title: Deploy Docker Compose with approval
recipes.summary: Require operator acknowledgement, pull pinned Compose images, start the stack, and record its status.
recipes.author: dagucloud
prerequisites: Docker Engine with Compose v2
A reviewed Compose project with pinned image versions
recipes.workflow:
description: Pull and deploy a Docker Compose project after explicit acknowledgement.

params:
  - name: project_dir
    default: /srv/app
  - name: compose_file
    default: compose.yaml

steps:
  - id: confirm
    action: human.task
    with:
      prompt: Acknowledge deployment of the Compose project in ${params.project_dir}

  - id: pull
    depends: [confirm]
    working_dir: ${params.project_dir}
    run: docker compose -f '${params.compose_file}' pull
    timeout_sec: 900

  - id: deploy
    depends: [pull]
    working_dir: ${params.project_dir}
    run: docker compose -f '${params.compose_file}' up -d --remove-orphans
    timeout_sec: 900

  - id: status
    depends: [deploy]
    working_dir: ${params.project_dir}
    run: docker compose -f '${params.compose_file}' ps
    stdout:
      artifact: compose-status.txt
recipes.readme:
# Deploy Docker Compose with approval

Pulls images and starts a Compose project after a human task is completed. The final Compose status is stored as a run artifact.

## Prerequisites

- Dagu 2.13.0 or newer and Docker Compose v2.
- A reviewed Compose project whose images use immutable versions or digests.

## Inputs and secrets

Configure `project_dir` and `compose_file`. Keep registry credentials in Docker's credential store rather than the workflow.

## What it changes

Pulls images, creates or replaces containers, and removes orphaned containers after acknowledgement.

## Verify

Review `compose-status.txt`, container health checks, application logs, and the service endpoint.

## Recovery

Restore the prior image tags or digest in the Compose file and rerun the workflow after acknowledgement.

recipes.title: Patch a Linux server fleet in batches
recipes.summary: Require operator acknowledgement and run a configurable patch command across SSH hosts with bounded concurrency.
recipes.author: dagucloud
prerequisites: SSH key authentication and known-host verification
Passwordless sudo for the selected patch command
Tested rollback or snapshot procedures
recipes.workflow:
description: Apply an approved patch command to a newline-separated list of hosts.

params:
  - name: hosts
    default: |
      server1.example.com
      server2.example.com
  - name: user
    default: deploy
  - name: key
    default: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
  - name: command
    default: sudo apt-get update && sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get upgrade -y

steps:
  - id: confirm
    action: human.task
    with:
      prompt: Review the host list and acknowledge the fleet patch operation

  - id: patch_hosts
    depends: [confirm]
    action: dag.run
    parallel:
      items: ${params.hosts}
      max_concurrent: 2
    with:
      dag: patch-host
      params:
        host: ${ITEM}
        user: ${params.user}
        key: ${params.key}
        command: ${params.command}
---
name: patch-host

params:
  - name: host
    required: true
  - name: user
    required: true
  - name: key
    required: true
  - name: command
    required: true

steps:
  - id: patch
    action: ssh.run
    with:
      host: ${params.host}
      user: ${params.user}
      key: ${params.key}
      shell: /bin/sh -e
      command: ${params.command}
recipes.readme:
# Patch a Linux server fleet in batches

Requires operator acknowledgement, then fans out a patch command to newline-separated SSH hosts with at most two concurrent child runs.

## Prerequisites

- Dagu 2.13.0 or newer.
- Key-based SSH access, verified host keys, passwordless sudo, and tested recovery procedures.

## Inputs and secrets

Review `hosts`, `user`, `key`, and `command` before every production use. The default command targets Debian-family systems.

## What it changes

Runs the configured package-manager command on every listed host after acknowledgement. Package upgrades can restart services or require a reboot.

## Verify

Inspect each child run, check package state and service health, and confirm whether any host requires a reboot.

## Recovery

Restore the affected host from its snapshot or package rollback procedure. Remove unhealthy hosts from the list before retrying.

recipes.title: Monitor an HTTP endpoint and alert Slack
recipes.summary: Check an HTTP endpoint on a schedule with retries and send a Slack webhook when the check fails.
recipes.author: dagucloud
prerequisites: A reachable HTTP endpoint
A Slack incoming webhook URL exposed through an environment-backed Dagu secret
recipes.workflow:
description: Check an HTTP endpoint and notify Slack when all retries fail.
schedule: "*/5 * * * *"

params:
  - name: url
    default: https://example.com/health

secrets:
  - name: SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL
    provider: env
    key: SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL

handler_on:
  failure:
    action: http.request
    with:
      method: POST
      url: ${env.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL}
      headers:
        Content-Type: application/json
      body: '{"text":"Dagu health check failed for ${params.url}. Run: ${context.run.id}"}'
      timeout: 10

steps:
  - id: health_check
    action: http.request
    with:
      method: GET
      url: ${params.url}
      timeout: 10
      silent: true
    retry_policy:
      limit: 3
      interval_sec: 10
recipes.readme:
# Monitor an HTTP endpoint and alert Slack

Checks an endpoint every five minutes. Dagu retries transient failures and sends one Slack webhook if the run still fails.

## Prerequisites

- Dagu 2.13.0 or newer.
- A Slack incoming webhook and network access to both endpoints.

## Inputs and secrets

Set `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` in the Dagu process environment. Override `url` and `timeout_seconds` for the monitored service.

## What it changes

Performs HTTP GET requests and, on failure, sends one message to Slack. It does not modify the monitored service.

## Verify

Run once against a healthy endpoint, then temporarily use a known failing URL and confirm the Slack notification.

## Recovery

Correct the endpoint or network issue and rerun the workflow. Remove the Slack webhook from the environment to disable notifications.

recipes.title: Monitor a scheduled job with Watchgoose
recipes.summary: Run a command and send start, success and failure pings to a Watchgoose check, which alerts when a run fails or never happens.
recipes.author: bartekrutkowski
prerequisites: A Watchgoose check
Its UUID or ping key and slug exposed through an environment-backed Dagu secret
recipes.workflow:
description: Run a scheduled job and report start, success and failure to a Watchgoose check.
schedule: "0 3 * * *"

params:
  - name: command
    default: /usr/local/bin/backup.sh
    description: Command to run. Scheduled runs use this default, so set it to your job.

# Report every failed run right away. With DAG-level retries (the base.yaml
# default), the failure handler and its fail ping wait for the last retry.
retry_policy:
  limit: 0

# The part of the check's ping URL after https://watchgoose.com/ping/:
# the check UUID, or <ping-key>/<slug>.
secrets:
  - name: WATCHGOOSE_CHECK
    provider: env
    key: WATCHGOOSE_CHECK

handler_on:
  success:
    action: http.request
    with:
      method: POST
      url: https://watchgoose.com/ping/${env.WATCHGOOSE_CHECK}
      body: "${context.dag.name} run ${context.run.id} ended with status ${context.run.status}."
      timeout: 10
      silent: true
  failure:
    action: http.request
    with:
      method: POST
      url: https://watchgoose.com/ping/${env.WATCHGOOSE_CHECK}/fail
      body: "${context.dag.name} run ${context.run.id} ended with status ${context.run.status}. Log: ${context.paths.log_file}"
      timeout: 10
      silent: true

steps:
  # A step, not an init handler: a failed init handler aborts the run, so an
  # unreachable monitor would stop the job itself.
  - id: ping_start
    action: http.request
    with:
      method: POST
      url: https://watchgoose.com/ping/${env.WATCHGOOSE_CHECK}/start
      timeout: 10
      silent: true
    continue_on:
      failure: true
      mark_success: true

  - id: job
    depends: [ping_start]
    run: ${params.command}
recipes.readme:
# Monitor a scheduled job with Watchgoose

Runs a command on a schedule and reports each run to a [Watchgoose](https://watchgoose.com) check. Watchgoose alerts you when a run fails, and also when a run never starts, for example because the Dagu host is down.

Each run sends two pings, `/start` and then either a success ping or `/fail`:

- `/start` before the command runs, so Watchgoose can measure run time.
- A success ping when the run succeeds.
- `/fail` when the run fails. The body names the run ID, status and log file path.

## Prerequisites

- Dagu 2.13.0 or newer.
- A Watchgoose check with a schedule and grace time that match the workflow's `schedule`.

## Inputs and secrets

Set `WATCHGOOSE_CHECK` in the Dagu process environment to the part of the check's ping URL after `https://watchgoose.com/ping/`:

- `<uuid>` for a UUID ping URL.
- `<ping-key>/<slug>` for a slug ping URL.

The workflow reads it as a Dagu secret, so it is masked in logs. Set the default of the `command` param to the job to run (scheduled runs use the default), and change `schedule` to match the check.

## What it changes

Runs `command` and sends up to two HTTPS requests per run to watchgoose.com. Nothing else.

`retry_policy.limit: 0` turns off DAG-level automatic retries for this workflow, so a failed run is reported at once. If you remove it and your `base.yaml` enables DAG retries, Dagu skips the failure handler until the last retry, so the fail ping comes later, and runs started with `dagu start` outside the scheduler never send it.

If Watchgoose cannot be reached, the start ping is ignored and the command still runs. A failed success or fail ping marks the run as failed in Dagu.

## Verify

Run once with a command that succeeds, then with one that fails:

```sh
dagu start workflow.yaml -- command="echo ok"
dagu start workflow.yaml -- command="false"
```

The check's event log in Watchgoose shows a start and a success ping, then a start and a failure ping.

## Recovery

Fix the command and rerun the workflow. The next success ping marks the check as up again.

recipes.title: Run a scheduled Kubernetes Job
recipes.summary: Replace a simple Kubernetes CronJob with a Dagu schedule and a version-pinned Job image.
recipes.author: dagucloud
prerequisites: Kubernetes credentials available to Dagu
A version-pinned container image and suitable service account
recipes.workflow:
description: Run a version-pinned container as a Kubernetes Job on a Dagu schedule.
schedule: "0 * * * *"

params:
  - name: namespace
    default: batch
  - name: image
    default: alpine:3.22.1
  - name: command
    default: echo 'replace this command with the batch job'

steps:
  - id: run_job
    action: kubernetes.run
    with:
      namespace: ${params.namespace}
      image: ${params.image}
      image_pull_policy: IfNotPresent
      command: ${params.command}
      cleanup_policy: delete
    timeout_sec: 1800
recipes.readme:
# Run a scheduled Kubernetes Job

Uses Dagu's scheduler and Kubernetes executor to create a Job, stream its logs, wait for completion, and clean it up.

## Prerequisites

- Dagu 2.13.0 or newer with access to the target cluster.
- A service account allowed to create, inspect, and delete Jobs and Pods.

## Inputs and secrets

Set `namespace`, a version-pinned `image`, and one `command`. Configure registry and application secrets through Kubernetes rather than embedding them in YAML.

## What it changes

Creates a Kubernetes Job and Pod on each scheduled run, then deletes them after completion.

## Verify

Review the Dagu run logs and confirm the expected external result of the batch command.

## Recovery

Suspend the Dagu workflow to stop future runs. Correct the image or command and rerun; completed Jobs are removed automatically.

recipes.title: Back up MySQL to S3
recipes.summary: Create a compressed, transaction-consistent MySQL dump and upload it to an S3-compatible bucket.
recipes.author: dagucloud
prerequisites: mysqldump and gzip
An S3-compatible bucket
MySQL and S3 credentials exposed through environment-backed Dagu secrets
recipes.workflow:
description: Create a compressed MySQL dump and upload it to S3.
schedule: "30 2 * * *"

params:
  - name: host
    default: 127.0.0.1
  - name: port
    type: integer
    default: 3306
    minimum: 1
    maximum: 65535
  - name: user
    default: backup
  - name: database
    required: true
  - name: bucket
    required: true
  - name: prefix
    default: mysql

secrets:
  - name: MYSQL_PASSWORD
    provider: env
    key: MYSQL_PASSWORD
  - name: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
    provider: env
    key: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
  - name: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    provider: env
    key: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

defaults:
  retry_policy:
    limit: 2
    interval_sec: 30

steps:
  - id: create_dump
    run: |
      #!/bin/sh
      set -eu
      timestamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
      file="$DAG_RUN_WORK_DIR/${params.database}-${timestamp}.sql.gz"
      key="${params.prefix}/${params.database}-${timestamp}.sql.gz"
      MYSQL_PWD="$MYSQL_PASSWORD" mysqldump \
        --single-transaction \
        --host="${params.host}" \
        --port="${params.port}" \
        --user="${params.user}" \
        "${params.database}" | gzip > "$file"
      printf 'file=%s\nkey=%s\n' "$file" "$key" >> "$DAGU_OUTPUT_FILE"
    outputs:
      - name: file
      - name: key

  - id: upload
    depends: [create_dump]
    action: s3.upload
    with:
      bucket: ${params.bucket}
      key: ${steps.create_dump.outputs.key}
      source: ${steps.create_dump.outputs.file}
      content_type: application/gzip
recipes.readme:
# Back up MySQL to S3

Creates a compressed `mysqldump` with a consistent transactional snapshot and uploads it to object storage.

## Prerequisites

- Dagu 2.13.0 or newer, `mysqldump`, and `gzip`.
- An S3-compatible bucket and a MySQL user with the required read privileges.

## Inputs and secrets

Set `MYSQL_PASSWORD`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` in the Dagu process environment. Provide `database` and `bucket`; review the connection parameters.

## What it changes

Writes a compressed dump in the run work directory and uploads one new object. It does not delete backups or modify MySQL data.

## Verify

Download a recent object, run `gzip -t`, and test a restore into a disposable database.

## Recovery

Decompress the selected object and restore it with the `mysql` client. Delete unwanted objects only after confirming retention requirements.

recipes.title: Back up PostgreSQL to S3
recipes.summary: Create a timestamped PostgreSQL dump and upload it to an S3-compatible bucket every night.
recipes.author: dagucloud
prerequisites: pg_dump
An S3-compatible bucket
Database and S3 credentials exposed through environment-backed Dagu secrets
recipes.workflow:
description: Create a PostgreSQL custom-format dump and upload it to S3.
schedule: "0 2 * * *"

params:
  - name: database_name
    default: app
    description: Safe name used in the backup filename
  - name: bucket
    required: true
    description: Destination S3 bucket
  - name: prefix
    default: postgres
    description: Object key prefix

secrets:
  - name: DATABASE_URL
    provider: env
    key: DATABASE_URL
  - name: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
    provider: env
    key: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
  - name: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    provider: env
    key: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

defaults:
  retry_policy:
    limit: 2
    interval_sec: 30

steps:
  - id: create_dump
    run: |
      #!/bin/sh
      set -eu
      timestamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
      file="$DAG_RUN_WORK_DIR/${params.database_name}-${timestamp}.dump"
      key="${params.prefix}/${params.database_name}-${timestamp}.dump"
      pg_dump --format=custom --file="$file" "$DATABASE_URL"
      printf 'file=%s\nkey=%s\n' "$file" "$key" >> "$DAGU_OUTPUT_FILE"
    outputs:
      - name: file
      - name: key

  - id: upload
    depends: [create_dump]
    action: s3.upload
    with:
      bucket: ${params.bucket}
      key: ${steps.create_dump.outputs.key}
      source: ${steps.create_dump.outputs.file}
      content_type: application/octet-stream
recipes.readme:
# Back up PostgreSQL to S3

Creates a custom-format `pg_dump` and uploads it to an S3-compatible bucket. Configure retention with the bucket lifecycle policy so the workflow never deletes backups itself.

## Prerequisites

- Dagu 2.13.0 or newer and `pg_dump` on the Dagu host.
- An S3-compatible bucket.

## Inputs and secrets

Set `DATABASE_URL`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` in the Dagu process environment. Provide `bucket`; optionally override `database_name` and `prefix`.

## What it changes

Writes a temporary dump in the run work directory and uploads one new object. It does not delete local or remote backups.

## Verify

Confirm that the uploaded object exists and periodically test a restore with `pg_restore --list` or a disposable database.

## Recovery

Download the selected object and restore it with `pg_restore`. Remove failed or unwanted objects through the storage provider after confirming they are not needed.

recipes.title: Restart a remote systemd service with approval
recipes.summary: Require operator acknowledgement, restart a service over SSH, and verify that it becomes active.
recipes.author: dagucloud
prerequisites: SSH key authentication and known-host verification
Permission to run systemctl for the selected service
recipes.workflow:
description: Restart a remote systemd service after explicit operator acknowledgement.

params:
  - name: host
    default: server.example.com
  - name: user
    default: deploy
  - name: service
    default: app.service
  - name: key
    default: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519

steps:
  - id: confirm
    action: human.task
    with:
      prompt: Acknowledge the restart of ${params.service} on ${params.host}

  - id: restart
    depends: [confirm]
    action: ssh.run
    with:
      host: ${params.host}
      user: ${params.user}
      key: ${params.key}
      command: sudo systemctl restart '${params.service}'

  - id: verify
    depends: [restart]
    action: ssh.run
    with:
      host: ${params.host}
      user: ${params.user}
      key: ${params.key}
      command: systemctl is-active '${params.service}'
    retry_policy:
      limit: 5
      interval_sec: 5
recipes.readme:
# Restart a remote systemd service with approval

Pauses for operator acknowledgement, restarts one systemd service over SSH, and retries the status check until the service is active or the run fails.

## Prerequisites

- Dagu 2.13.0 or newer.
- Key-based SSH access with host-key verification and permission to run `systemctl`.

## Inputs and secrets

Configure `host`, `user`, `service`, and the SSH `key` path. No password is stored in the workflow.

## What it changes

Restarts the selected remote service only after a human task is completed.

## Verify

The final step runs `systemctl is-active`. Also verify the service health endpoint and recent journal entries.

## Recovery

Inspect `journalctl -u <service>`, restore the prior service configuration or release, and restart again after approval.

recipes.title: Transfer an SFTP file to S3
recipes.summary: Download a file over SFTP into the isolated run directory and upload it to an S3-compatible bucket.
recipes.author: dagucloud
prerequisites: SSH key authentication and known-host verification
An S3-compatible bucket
S3 credentials exposed through environment-backed Dagu secrets
recipes.workflow:
description: Download one SFTP file and upload it to S3.
schedule: "0 * * * *"

params:
  - name: host
    default: files.example.com
  - name: user
    default: ingest
  - name: key
    default: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
  - name: remote_file
    default: /exports/latest.csv
  - name: bucket
    required: true
  - name: object_key
    default: incoming/latest.csv

secrets:
  - name: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
    provider: env
    key: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
  - name: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    provider: env
    key: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

steps:
  - id: download
    action: sftp.download
    with:
      host: ${params.host}
      user: ${params.user}
      key: ${params.key}
      source: ${params.remote_file}
      destination: ${context.paths.work_dir}/incoming.dat

  - id: upload
    depends: [download]
    action: s3.upload
    with:
      bucket: ${params.bucket}
      key: ${params.object_key}
      source: ${context.paths.work_dir}/incoming.dat
recipes.readme:
# Transfer an SFTP file to S3

Downloads one remote file into the isolated run directory, then uploads it to object storage.

## Prerequisites

- Dagu 2.13.0 or newer.
- Key-based SFTP access with host-key verification and an S3-compatible bucket.

## Inputs and secrets

Configure the SFTP connection, `remote_file`, `bucket`, and `object_key`. Set `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` in the Dagu process environment.

## What it changes

Reads the SFTP file, writes a temporary local copy, and creates or replaces the selected S3 object. It does not delete the SFTP source.

## Verify

Compare file size or checksum between the SFTP source and the uploaded object before downstream processing.

## Recovery

Correct credentials or paths and rerun. Restore an overwritten object from bucket versioning when enabled.

recipes.title: Alert before a TLS certificate expires
recipes.summary: Check a remote TLS certificate daily and notify Slack when its remaining lifetime falls below a threshold.
recipes.author: dagucloud
prerequisites: openssl
Network access to the TLS endpoint
A Slack incoming webhook URL exposed through an environment-backed Dagu secret
recipes.workflow:
description: Fail and notify Slack when a TLS certificate expires too soon.
schedule: "0 8 * * *"

params:
  - name: host
    default: example.com
  - name: port
    type: integer
    default: 443
    minimum: 1
    maximum: 65535
  - name: minimum_days
    type: integer
    default: 21
    minimum: 1
    maximum: 365

secrets:
  - name: SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL
    provider: env
    key: SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL

handler_on:
  failure:
    action: http.request
    with:
      method: POST
      url: ${env.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL}
      headers:
        Content-Type: application/json
      body: '{"text":"TLS certificate check failed for ${params.host}:${params.port}; fewer than ${params.minimum_days} days may remain."}'

steps:
  - id: check_certificate
    run: |
      #!/bin/sh
      set -eu
      seconds="$(( ${params.minimum_days} * 86400 ))"
      openssl s_client \
        -connect "${params.host}:${params.port}" \
        -servername "${params.host}" \
        </dev/null 2>/dev/null \
        | openssl x509 -checkend "$seconds" -noout
    retry_policy:
      limit: 2
      interval_sec: 30
recipes.readme:
# Alert before a TLS certificate expires

Uses `openssl` to verify that a remote certificate remains valid for the configured number of days. A failed check triggers a Slack webhook.

## Prerequisites

- Dagu 2.13.0 or newer and `openssl`.
- A Slack incoming webhook.

## Inputs and secrets

Set `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` in the Dagu process environment. Configure `host`, `port`, and `minimum_days`.

## What it changes

Opens a TLS connection and may send one Slack message. It does not alter the certificate or endpoint.

## Verify

Run against the production hostname, then raise `minimum_days` temporarily to confirm that the alert path works.

## Recovery

Renew or replace the certificate, verify the served certificate chain, and rerun the workflow.
